name: Cintas Corporation

R1.just: Route-based uniform rental scales with density (more stops per route lowers unit cost), but it is a physical-logistics model with ~17% FCF margin, not software/network operating leverage, so no 1.5-2.0.

R2.just: Uniform rental/facility services grows with employment and outsourcing penetration; +8% organic FY25 shows secular tailwind but it is a GDP-plus, not high-growth, end market.

R3.just: Clear #1 in North American uniform rental with ~$10.3B revenue, multiples larger than Aramark/UniFirst, sustained leadership though not pure monopoly so short of 2.0.

R4.just: Moat from route density, switching costs (embedded service/garment inventory), brand and scale; durable but replicable over decades by a well-capitalized challenger, so 1.5 not 2.0.

R5.just: FY25 organic growth +8% (Q3 FY26 organic +8.2%) shows growth is overwhelmingly organic, not M&A-driven, earning above-base credit.

R6.just: Over 1 million customers with no single client near 10%, broad SMB/enterprise and end-market diversification across uniforms, first aid, fire protection.

R7.just: ROIC ~26.9% far above WACC, FCF $1.757B = ~17% margin, FCF/NI healthy; capital intensity of laundry plants offset by superior returns earns above-base.

R8.just: ND/EBITDA ~0.97x and net debt $2.73B is modest and well under 2x, but not net cash, so base score.

R9.just: SBC verified at only 7.3% of FCF (1.24% of revenue), well below the 15% hard-rule threshold, so no penalty and accounting looks clean.

R10.just: Long track record of disciplined capital allocation, consistent buybacks and dividend growth, organic-first vs destructive M&A, raised FY26 guidance signaling execution credibility.

amplification_note: R3 (#1 leader) and R4 (density/switching-cost moat) reinforce each other strongly, but R1 is only base (physical logistics model, not software/network operating leverage), so the trio does not reach the monstrous, irreplicable mutual reinforcement required for amplification.
moat_one_line: Route density plus high switching costs (embedded uniform inventory, recurring service contracts) and brand scale make the #1 North American uniform-rental operator hard to dislodge.
thesis_3lines: Calidad: lider #1 indiscutido en alquiler de uniformes con ROIC ~27%, foso de densidad de rutas y altos costes de cambio, SBC minima (7.3% del FCF) y balance solido (ND/EBITDA ~0.97x).
Crecimiento: motor organico +8% con penetracion creciente del outsourcing, cross-selling (first aid, fire protection) y direccion que SUBIO la guia FY26 a EPS ajustado $4.86-4.90 (+10-11%).
Valoracion: fwd P/E ~32x (-14% vs su media 5a de ~37.5) tras caida ~25% por rotacion/miedo, no deterioro; PEG 2.87 sigue exigente, retorno depende de compounding sostenido mas que de re-rating.
bear_case_strongest: A pesar de la caida del 25%, el fwd P/E ~32x y PEG 2.87 siguen siendo premium para un compounder GDP-plus cuyo crecimiento organico se desacelera con el empleo, exponiendo la accion a mayor compresion de multiplo si la macro laboral se debilita.
notes: Total re-score = 13.0/13.5 (R1 1.0, R2 1.0, R3 1.5, R4 1.5, R5 1.5, R6 1.5, R7 1.5, R8 1.0, R9 1.0, R10 1.5). Slight downgrade from preliminary 13.5 because R1 (no software/network operating leverage) and R2 (GDP-plus, not high-growth secular) and R8 (not net cash) are base-level, not superior. SBC hard rule passed comfortably (7.3% of FCF < 15%). Valuation multiples, ROIC, net debt and SBC ratios are ESTIMADO from StockAnalysis.com aggregator; last_q, last_fy organic growth, FCF and guidance are VERIFIED from Cintas IR/SEC. Drop classified fear_rotation (multiple compression from peak fwd P/E ~53), not operating deterioration.
